FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Automotive Body and Chassis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. In preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been derived from BS AU 209 Vehicle Security, Part 7 Specification for locking systems for goods vehicle driving components, ARAI Safety Standard No. 311993, SAE J 838 Vehicle passenger - Door hinge systems and SAE J 839 Passenger car side door latch system. The committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex C. In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`,

IS 14225 : 1995

Indian Standard

AUTOMOTIVEVEHICLES-LOCKING SYSTEMSANDDOORRETENTION COMPONENTS -GENERALREQUIREMENTS
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies requirements for side door including emergency door locks and side door retention components including latches, hinges and other supporting means, fitted on cars, light and heavy commercial vehicles to minimize the likelihood of occupants being thrown out from the vehicle as a result of any impact. 1.2 This standard does not apply to those vehicles which are not normally provided with a door. 2 TERMINOLOGY 2.1 Cargo Type Door Cargo-type door means a door designed primarily to accommodate cargo loading including but not limited to a two-part door that latches to itself. 2.2 Side Front Door Side front door means a door that, in a side view, has 50 percent or more of its opening area forward of the rearmost point on the driver's seatback, when the driver's seat is adjusted to its most vertical and rearward position. 2.3 Side Rear Door Side rear door means a door that, in a side view, has more than 50 percent of its opening area to the rear of the rearmost point on the driver's seatback, when the drivers's seat is adjusted to its most vertical and rearward position. 2.4 Latch A mechanical device employed to position the door in a closed position relative to the vehicle body with provision for controlled release ( or operation ). 2.4 1 Latch Components 2.4.1.1 Plate The main body or frame for supporting working components, appendages and transmitting or distributing loads to the door structure. 1 2.4.1.2 Rotor ( Bolts ) The rotating or sliding member of the latch which engages and restrains the latch to the striker. 2.4.1.3 Ratchet A member of the latch connected to the rotor to provide an abutment or abutments which, when properly indexed, become engaged with a related paw1 to prevent motion of the rotor in one direction. 2.4.1.4 Paw1 A member of the latch that can be operated to engage the abutments of the ratchet to prevent relative motion between the two parts except in one direction. 2.5 Striker A mechanical device with which the latch engages on the opposing member or the body. 2.6 Fully Latched Position The position that exists between the latch and striker when the door is secured in the fully closed position. 2.7 Secondary Latched Position The position that exists between the latch and striker when the latch holds the door in a partially closed position.
NOTEThe secondary latched position may be included in the side door latch, as an added mechanical feature to reduce the possibility of the door opening freely, in the event the door is not closed to the fully latched position. It shall be recognized that doors are intended to be in the fully latched position whenever the vehicle is in motion.

3 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS Following components on any side door leading directly into a compartment that contains one or more seating accommodations shall conform to this standard and shall pass the tests as per test procedures in 4.

3.2.1 3.2.1.1 Door Latches Longitudinal load

Each door latch and striker assembly provided with two positions consisting a) A fully latched position, and b) A secondary latched position.
3.1.1.1 Longitudinal load

shall be of:

Each latch system, when in the latched position, shall not separate when a longitudinal load of 1 135 kgf is applied. 3.2.1.2 Transverse load Each latch system, when in the latched tion shall not separate when a transverse of 910 kgf is applied. When more than latch system is used on a single door, the requirement may be divided among the number of latch systems. 3.2.2 Door Hinges Each door hinge system shall support the door and shall not separate when a longitudinal load of 1 135 kgf is applied and when a transverse load of 9`0 kgf is applied. 3.3 Sliding Doors The track and slide combination or other supporting means for each sliding door shall not when a total transverse load of separate 1 820 kti is applied, with the door in the closed position. 4 TEST PROCEDURES 4.1 Hinged
Doors ) 4.1.1 Door Latches 4.1.1.1 Longitudinal and tranwerse loads

The door latch and striker assembly, when in the fully latched position, shall not separate when a longitudinal load of 1 135 kgf is applied. In the secondary latched position, the door latch and striker assembly shall not separate when a longitudinal load of 455 kgf is applied. 3.1.1.2 Transverse load The door latch and striker assembly, when in the fully latched position, shall not separate when a transverse load of 910 kgf is applied. In the secondary latched position, the door latch and striker assembly shall not separate when a transverse load of 455 kfg is applied. 3.1.1.3 Inertia load The door latch shall nof disengage from the fully latched position when a longitudinal or transverse inertia load of 30 g is applied to the door latch system ( including the latch and its actuating mechanism with the locking mechanism disengaged ). 3.1.2 Door Hinges Each door hinge system shall support the door and shall not separate when a longitudinal load of 1 135 kgf is applied. Similarly, each door hinge system shall not separate when a tranverse load of 910 kgf is applied. 3.1.2.1 Hinges shall be mounted at the front edge of the door in the direction of forward travel. 3.1.3 Each door except the driver's door, shall be equipped with a locking mechanism with means of operating from the interior of the vehicle. 3.1.3.1 Driver's side door

The testing may be performed either on the vehicle or with the door retention components in a bench fixture.

TEST REQUIREMENTS FOR HINGED DOORS AND LATCHES A-l REQUIREMENTS A-l.1 Longitudinal Load A door latch and striker assembly, when tested as described under test procedures, shall be able to withstand an ultimate longitudinal load of 1 135 kgf when in the fully latched position and 455 kgf when in the secondary latched position. A-l.2 Transverse Load A-2.1.2 Equipment a) Tensile testing machine b) Static test fixture ( see Fig. 1 ) A-2.1.3 Operation a) Attach the test fixture to the mounting provisions of the latch and striker. Align the direction of engagement parallel to the linkage of the fixture. Mount fixture with latch and striker in fully latched position in the test machine so as to apply a load perpendicular to the face of the latch. b) Locate weights to apply a 90 kgf load tending to separate the latch and striker in the direction of the door opening. c) Apply the test load at a rate not exceeding 5 mm per minute until failure occurred or till 1 135 kgf. Record maximum load. A-2.2 Longitudinal Position ) A-2.2.1 Purpose To determine the ability of the vehicle latch and striker in the secondary position to withstand a test load perpendicular to the face of t,,e latch A.2.2.2 Test Equipment a) Tensile testing machine b) Static test fixture ( see Fig. 1 ) 3 Load ( Secondary Latched

A-l.3 Inertia Load A door latch system ( including the door latch, striker assembly, outside handle, kev cvlinder and any connection mechanisms ) i'n the fully latched position, when evaluated by calculation, shall remain in the fully latched position when subjected to an inertia load of 30 g in any direction. IS 14225 : 1995 A-3 INFRTIAL LOAD ANALYSIS ( MATHEMATICAL ) A-3.1 Purpose To determine the ability of the vehicle latch system to resist inertia loading by mzans of a mathematical analysis of the component parts in actual mounting on a car.
NOTE - Due to the complexity of physical testing for iriertial characteristics it is more practical and more accurate to base evaluations on mathematical analysis. The procedure described in this section provides a means for analytically determining the ability of a door latch system to withstand inertia loading. Spring forces are the average of the minimum spring output in tb- installed position and the minimum spring output in the release position. Frictioo effects and work to be done are not considered in the calculations. Gravitational pull on components may also be omitted if it tends to restrict unlatching. These omissions from the calculations are permissible because they provide additional factors of safety.

ANNEX B ( Clauses 4.1.2 and 4.2.2
TEST REQUIREMENTS B-l REQUIREMENTS B-l.1 Longitudinal Load A vehicle passenger door hinge system, when tested as piescribed under test procedure in B-2.1, must be capable of withstanding an ultimate longitudinal load of 1 135 kgf. B-l.2 Transverse Load A vehicle passenger door hinge system, when tested in accordance with the test procedure in B-2.1, must be capable of withstanding an ultimate transverse load of 910 kgf.
